text:
alex: noticing a bunch of 503s for acme-prod around 12:02 UTC, customer complaining about timeouts

maria: looking now, seeing upstream errors from inference pool, rolling 5xx spike in the hosted gateway

alex: gateway logs: "upstream request failed: http: upstream exited unexpectedly (signal 11)" repeated

jit: pulling runner logs for the affected host, starting with pod infer-runner-7b9c in pool-hosted-03

jit: logs show repeated OOMs during batched streaming, then segfault: `worker crashed: signal 11 (SIGSEGV)`

maria: can you paste the exact snippet? we need to know if it's CUDA OOM or CPU OOM on prefetch

jit: paste follows:
```
[2026-03-18T12:02:17Z] infer-runner[pid:2345] ERROR: Caught cudaErrorOutOfMemory, attempting graceful shutdown
[2026-03-18T12:02:17Z] infer-runner[pid:2345] INFO: freeing KV cache pages for context=acme-prod
[2026-03-18T12:02:18Z] infer-runner[pid:2345] SEGV at 0x0 (pc=0x7f3a2c12)
[2026-03-18T12:02:18Z] kernel: process 2345 (infer-runner) killed by SIGSEGV
```

alex: that looks like OOM then a segfault while falling back, we've seen similar when batch size autoscaling pushes too many contexts to the same GPU

maria: checking autoscaler events and recent config changes — no manual changes in the last 24h, but there was a sudden embed-heavy burst from client auth-service at ~12:01

support: opened a customer ticket (CS-9821) and informed acme that we're investigating. they reported sessions dropped and a few failed requests in the UI

luis: assigning to eng-infra for kernel-level debugging, and eng-runtime for runner-level fixes. tagging @maria and @jit

sre-bot: incident created INC-20260318-1, priority P1, notify: eng-runtime, eng-infra, support

maria: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) scale up GPU pool size for acme-prod (add preemptible workers) 2) reduce max batch size for streaming routes 3) add KV cache eviction to free memory earlier

jit: repro steps I ran locally (repro with synthetic load):
1) start infer-runner with model=redwood-13b-quant on node with 40GB GPU
2) send concurrent streaming requests with context size ~120k tokens and concurrency 60 hitting batching window 50ms
3) observe memory climb -> OOM at ~52 concurrent streams

jit: command used: `aburst --concurrency 60 --stream --ctx 120000 --route /v1/stream` (internal loadtool)

alex: good repro. for short-term rollback we can pin acme to a smaller model variant or lower batch cap via routing policy

maria: I'm going to push an autoscaler override to temporarily cap pool concurrency and reduce per-worker batch cap to 16. applying now.

maria: applied: `pool.acme-prod.max_concurrency=40` and `runner.batch.max_tokens=16384`

maria: monitoring... error rate dropped to baseline within 90s :thumbsup:

support: customer updated: they see improvements, but asked for root cause and ETA for a permanent fix

luis: next steps for permanent: (a) add guard rails in batching logic to avoid oversubscription during auth/burst patterns, (b) improve OOM fallback path so it doesn't segfault when freeing KV cache, (c) add more granular per-customer memory telemetry

jit: I will open runtime PR with extra checks before KV cache touch and add safe-free path + unit test.

maria: eng-infra to look at kernel SIGSEGV traces and see if driver interactions are contributing; also collect full coredump from node if available

alex: please add repro artifacts to the incident (loadtool script, exact runner config, kernel oops) so SRE can keep for postmortem

sre-bot: added runbook: "hotpath oom -> segfault mitigation" to INC-20260318-1

luis: tagging for postmortem: hold a 30m post-incident at 16:00 UTC today; agenda: root cause, mitigations, release plan

support: closing the loop with customer: shared mitigation and timeline. they requested notification when the permanent fix is live

maria: assigning owners: jit (runtime fix), eng-infra (kernel trace) -> target milestone: next patch release (2 business days)

alex: thanks all — great cross-team response. leaving this thread open for updates, will update CS when the patch lands.
